note: Other ships you can see (scripts/flight/traffic.gd) and derelicts to salvage. Counts follow the economy's carriers in the system, capped. Distances in metres, speeds in m/s. pods: station shuttles; survey: exploration craft among the movers; orbiters: ships circling the planet and its neighbour; deep: derelicts out along a run's route, ships whose FTL failed mid-route. hold: what's behind a derelict's cargo hatch (scripts/salvage.gd).

names: a long-hauler with no name on it

hold.note: A derelict's cargo hatch: torch it open (cut_s), then haul out what's inside one item at a time (grab_s). Crates and parts need room in your hold; parts sell at the shipyard for cost x condition x part_rate; cargo sells to a buyer at the port at its quote x buyer_rate, or scrap_rate of base value if nobody here takes it. A salvaged part can be fitted in the shipyard instead: fit_rate of its new price (at least fit_min_cr), keeping its wear (1 - condition).

boarding.note: Going inside a derelict (scripts/flight/boarding.gd, scripts/wreckage.gd): its airlock's outer door is cut with the torch (door_cut_s), then you walk it on mag boots and suit air. What's aboard is rolled per wreck: crew, each a survivor (rare), dead or long gone in the pod; crates in the holds, a locker or two, the flight recorder at the helm and the log. Handed in at a port's freight office: recorders to the insurer for recorder_bounty, remains to the port authority for recovery_fee each (remains_t of hold space each), survivors for rescue_bounty and rescue_rep standing, after which they'll sign on with no fee. Every ship has a jump seat for one rescued person beyond its bunks; past that, a survivor is reported instead (the port sends its own boat) for finder_share of the bounty and finder_rep standing.

jump: Jump drive tripped out halfway across. We're nowhere. The nav computer agrees, at length.
Spooled the drive twice more. It just hums now. Beacon's on.
Nobody's answered the beacon. The lanes are quiet out here. That's why we took them.
reactor: Reactor scrammed coming off the burn. Batteries say twelve hours if we're careful.
We weren't careful. Heaters off in the holds.
Beacon's on. If anyone's listening, the coffee's in the galley locker. It's terrible.
breach: Debris strike aft. Lost pressure in the back half before the doors closed.
Patched what we could reach. Couldn't reach enough.
Beacon's on. Whoever finds this: the hull plates by the hold are the good ones.
dry: Tanks dry. Somebody did the fuel sums on the back of a ration pack. Somebody was me.
Drifting. The station's lights are right there. Right there.
Beacon's on. Tell the company the cargo's fine. They'll ask.

boarding.evacuated_line: {names} took the pod. Said they'd send someone. I'm sure they meant it.
boarding.dead_line: {names} didn't make it. We've laid them out in the {room}. Somebody should take them home.
boarding.survivor_line: {name} is in the cold bunk. If you're reading this, so might they be.
boarding.last_line: Last entry. Leaving the log running for whoever comes.
